title: Chapter 75: Mu Yang High School
html:
A child’s thinking is more direct and less metaphorical. Could this drawing be an actual representation of the crime scene that he witnessed?

The house is black, meaning the time of the crime was at night, and the people inside the house are red—they probably represent his parents, the victims. This is the most direct interpretation.

Chen Ge examined the drawing from every angle. Fan Yu’s hurried style gave each human figure the same featureless shape; their genders were impossible to determine.

Wait. The red figures probably aren’t his parents; there are far too many.Chen Ge tried to count them, but the tangled lines yielded a different total each time. It’s too chaotic. What is Fan Yu trying to communicate?

Fan Yu had drawn the same scene over and over: a black house crowded with red people. Yet every time he finished, he crumpled the paper and threw it aside, dissatisfied.

Whatever it means, this drawing is an important clue.Even after studying it at length, Chen Ge reached no conclusion. He slipped the paper into his pocket and glanced back at the building. The door he had left ajar was now closed.

The aunt and the child are both troubling in their own ways. The question is… which one is hiding more?After finding his way out of the maze-like alleys, Chen Ge boarded the bus. If the woman had told the truth, that night’s mission would be extraordinarily dangerous.

To prepare, Chen Ge searched online for more information about Mu Yang High School. He found a surprising amount, most of it scattered across school forums.

Judging by the dates, many posters had attended Mu Yang High School before its closure. Forced to transfer elsewhere, they had carried the school’s legends with them.

Several posts caught Chen Ge’s attention. About a year earlier, five students had entered Mu Yang High School on a dare. Rather than record video, they documented the excursion by updating a thread every few minutes.

The original thread had long since been deleted, but Chen Ge found a repost. According to the account, the students entered the sealed classroom and attempted to summon the Pen Spirit.

The five sat around a table to perform the ritual. By the time the game ended, seven people stood in the classroom. No one knew where the other two had come from. The five students fled the school screaming and in tears.

All five survived, but two emerged profoundly changed. One became violently unstable; the other developed an irrational terror of daylight. Both eventually moved away from Jiujiang.

In the comments, one poster drew a connection: two extra people had appeared during the ritual, and two students afterward behaved strangely. Perhaps the pair who escaped were no longer the original students, who remained trapped in the classroom.

The theory received many likes, though others disagreed. Some claimed all five had been possessed, but only the two strong enough to resist displayed obvious symptoms.

A teacher had pinned a notice forbidding further discussion of Mu Yang High School. Scrolling farther, Chen Ge discovered a hidden reply.

Its contents baffled him. The poster claimed that his father’s company had planned to purchase the Mu Yang High School property at a low price. Everything proceeded normally until the contract neared completion. Then his father began dreaming every night that students in Mu Yang High School uniforms came to their home for lessons.

More disturbing, each morning they found signs of forced entry. The father grew so frightened that he fell ill and eventually resigned. The account ended there.

As he read the posts, Chen Ge compared Mu Yang High School with Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy and noticed something strange.

The internet teemed with supernatural stories about Mu Yang High School, but none involved death or serious injury. Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy had inspired far fewer rumors, yet police records documented multiple deaths there.

When you think about it, Western Jiujiang’s Private Academy sounds much worse.It was the only reassurance Chen Ge could offer himself.

Sitting on the bus and looking out the window, Chen Ge’s phone suddenly rang. He looked down and saw it was from He San.

The kid sensed the possible unlocking of a new scenario, so he called to book in advance?Chen Ge answered the call and placed his phone beside his ear. “Hello?”

“Boss, quickly get on the video-sharing app, someone is coming for your bread and butter!”

“Huh? Did someone open a new Haunted House?” Chen Ge launched the app. Before the home page loaded, an advertisement filled the screen: ‘Host Qin Guang Leads You Inside a Real Haunted House!’

Chen Ge clicked on the screen and more details popped up.

Qin Guang was a famous streamer with more than six hundred thousand followers, best known for humorous short videos. His profile listed XX Studio—the same company that had tried to recruit Chen Ge after Ping An Apartments.

According to the advertisement, Qin Guang was branching into new territory with a mystery livestream from a genuinely haunted location.

At first, Chen Ge thought little of it. Then he saw Qin Guang’s first mystery location and fell silent: Qin Guang’s team planned to stream from Ping An Apartments in western Jiujiang.

“Boss, have you seen it? That man realized that you had more than ten thousand views on your first livestream, so he’s trying to copy your formula!” He San grumbled indignantly.

“There’s no need to worry, certain things cannot be copied.”

Chen Ge had expected important news and was disappointed. Qin Guang did not worry him, though he knew the famous host would not regard him as competition either.

On the other end of the phone, He San said urgently, “He has so many followers. After he consolidates himself as a supernatural host, I’m afraid they’ll turn around and claim that it was you who copied them!”

“It’ll be fine. By the way, are you familiar with child psychology? I have a few questions for you.”

“Boss, at a time like this, how can you worry about that? Besides, I study forensic medicine. If you have psychology questions, ask a psychologist or psychiatrist!”
